facts.text: Woodlake sits on the western shore of a 1,700‑acre Swift Creek Reservoir, a man‑made lake built in 1965 to supply water.
East West Communities began building Woodlake in 1984, and the first homes appeared in 1985, turning farmland into a master‑planned lakefront community.
In 1990, the Urban Land Institute named Woodlake the “Best Community in America” for its innovative planning and quality‑of‑life features.
The community’s nonprofit homeowners’ association, the WCA, manages the reservoir and hosts events like a Military Honor Garden fundraiser.
Woodlake’s climate is humid subtropical, with July highs around 90°F and January lows near 28°F, and it averages 44 inches of rain yearly.
The area was originally part of the Powhatan Confederacy’s traditional lands before European settlers arrived in 1611 with Henricus.
